parsed.explanation: The write-up explicitly admits this step still “Need[s]” proof, and none appears later. Moreover, the assertion is false. For n=2, Liu’s proposed pieces are 2/5, 2/5, 1/5. Xiang may use both cuts on the 1/5 piece, dividing it into 1/10, 1/20, 1/20. The sorted final lengths are 2/5, 2/5, 1/10, 1/20, 1/20, so Liu receives the odd-ranked pieces totaling 2/5+1/10+1/20=11/20<3/5. Thus responses other than splitting each big piece once can indeed reduce Liu’s share, invalidating the proposed all-n lower bound.
